Mating components in a pilot batch

Pilot batches and high-mix, low-volume projects bridging prototypes and production.

Typical geometry
Structural housings, cylindrical features, mating faces and bores.
Material options
Aluminum and cast-blank machining options. Confirm the material for each part.
Key review
List the parts and shared assembly interfaces in the pilot batch. Identify which items need milling, turning or cast-blank machining.
Request a quote

Have a drawing? Add it to your inquiry email.

Manufacturing options
Materials
Aluminum and cast-blank machining options. Confirm the material for each part.
Machining
CNC milling, turning, 5-axis machining and secondary casting machining.
Surface finish
Coordinate finish requirements with each material and part revision.

Made to order. Your approved drawing and quotation define the specification; the image is not a material certificate, dimensional record or inspection result.

inspection requirements

Geometry & interfaces
Give each item a part number, revision, material and quantity; identify shared interfaces across the assembly.
Material & finish
Specify the material grade, condition, finish and any masked areas.
Quantity
State the prototype or batch quantity and required schedule.
Inspection requirements
Agree first-article checks and subsequent sampling for each part. One unspecified batch requirement is insufficient.
